concepts.def: Mass per unit volume: ρ = m ÷ V, measured in kg/m³.
Solids have fixed, closely-packed particles; liquids are close but free to move; gases are far apart and move randomly.
The energy needed to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1°C: Q = m × c × Δθ.
The energy needed to change the state of 1 kg of a substance with no change in temperature: Q = m × L.
Gas particles collide with the container walls; faster or more frequent collisions create greater pressure.
For a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ — pressure is inversely proportional to volume.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Solids, Liquids & Gases — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Solids, Liquids & Gases brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Solids, Liquids & Gases.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: An ideal gas at constant volume has its absolute temperature doubled. Its pressure:
options: Halves
Stays the same
Doubles
Quadruples
V/T = constant
pV = constant
p/T = constant
pV/T = constant

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the activity of a source and the dose received by a person?
options: Activity and dose are the same — both measure how dangerous the radiation is.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Activity is for nuclear power stations and dose is for medical X-rays.
Activity (Bq) is the rate of nuclear decays in the source; dose (Sv) measures the biological effect of absorbed radiation on tissue.

mcqs.q: Which type of nuclear radiation is most ionising?
options: Alpha radiation — large, doubly charged particles cause the most ionisation per unit distance.
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Gamma is most ionising because it can travel furthest and pass through almost anything.

mcqs.q: Why does light bend when it enters a denser medium like glass?
options: Because the medium is denser, it physically blocks part of the light and forces it to turn.
Because it slows down — the change in speed at the boundary causes the wavefront to bend (towards the normal).
Beta radiation is most ionising because it consists of fast electrons.
Because gravity in the glass pulls the light down.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Avogadro constant”?
options: At constant temperature, pV = constant for a fixed mass of gas.
pV = nRT, relating pressure, volume, amount and temperature for an ideal gas.
N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, the number of particles in one mole.
<c²>, average of the squared speeds of particles; related to temperature by ½m<c²> = (3/2)kT.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Charles's law”?
options: At constant pressure, V/T = constant for a fixed mass of gas.
N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, the number of particles in one mole.
pV = nRT, relating pressure, volume, amount and temperature for an ideal gas.
p = (1/3)(Nm/V)<c²>, derived from collisions of molecules with container walls.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Mean square speed”?
options: At constant temperature, pV = constant for a fixed mass of gas.
pV = nRT, relating pressure, volume, amount and temperature for an ideal gas.
At constant pressure, V/T = constant for a fixed mass of gas.
<c²>, average of the squared speeds of particles; related to temperature by ½m<c²> = (3/2)kT.
